key_findings_zh: 有强有力的证据表明,在 COVID-19 期间,狂犬病 控制活动减少,导致贾夫纳的动物咬伤和 狂犬病 病例增加。狗 疫苗接种 覆盖率的增加与人类 狂犬病 死亡人数的减少相关。大多数 狂犬病 死亡 (93%) 发生在从事经济活动的成年人中,其中 64% 是男性,病例集中在瓦利卡马姆和瓦达马拉奇地区。 [10.4038/jmj.v38i1.257]

66.7% 的患者和 62.9% 的患者将浸润难易程度评为“容易”(p = 0.63)。局部不良事件并不常见,疼痛发生率分别为 2.5% 和 7.5% (p = 0.07),红斑发生率≤ 1.3%。没有发生严重的全身不良事件。Rabishield 每位患者需要更多药瓶(2.28 ± 0.84 vs 2.00 ± 0.69;p = 0.001),并且平均浸润体积较高(4.7 ± 1.9 mL vs 4.0 ± 1.6 mL;p < 0.001),而组间浪费相似(1.03 ± 0.72 mL vs 1.03 ± 0.69 mL;p = 0.95)。 [10.1371/journal.pntd.0014274]
单克隆抗体 (mAb) 是 RIG 的有效且经济的替代品。此外,最近的临床前研究提供的证据表明单克隆抗体可以有效治疗有症状的 狂犬病,克服病毒免疫逃避机制。 [10.1016/j.molmed.2026.06.014]
顺行追踪揭示了共享的和特定通路的二阶目标,包括双向 CA1v 预测。逆行追踪证实了预期的输入,例如 CA3,并确定了以前未识别的皮质来源,这些来源在 CA1v 亚群中存在差异。 [10.1007/s00429-026-03164-y]
对符合纳入标准的 89 例病例进行了分析;只有 3 例被归类为“真正的”突破性感染。 [10.1093/cid/ciaf662]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: There is strong evidence that rabies control activities were reduced during COVID-19, leading to increased animal bites and rabies cases in Jaffna. Increased dog vaccination coverage correlated with reduced human rabies deaths. [10.4038/jmj.v38i1.257]

Ease of infiltration was rated "easy" in 66.7% versus 62.9% of patients (p = 0.63). Local adverse events were uncommon, with pain reported in 2.5% versus 7.5% (p = 0.07) and erythema in ≤ 1.3% of participants. No serious systemic adverse events occurred. [10.1371/journal.pntd.0014274]

Monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) represent an effective and economical alternative to RIGs. Moreover, recent preclinical studies have provided evidence that monoclonal antibodies can effectively treat symptomatic rabies, overcoming mechanisms of viral immune evasion. [10.1016/j.molmed.2026.06.014]

Anterograde tracing revealed shared and pathway-specific second-order targets, including bidirectional CA1v projections. Retrograde tracing confirmed expected inputs such as CA3 and identified previously unrecognized cortical sources that varied across CA1v subpopulations. [10.1007/s00429-026-03164-y]
Eighty-nine cases fulfilling the inclusion criteria were analyzed; only 3 were classified as "true" breakthrough infections. [10.1093/cid/ciaf662]
literature.trend_or_risk_en: The direction of this week's research is defined by the clinical, epidemiological, ecological, diagnostic and molecular topics actually represented by the eligible publications.
literature.brief_en: This literature brief prioritizes papers published in the active reporting window and ranks them by relevance, evidence availability, study quality, recency, and independent-source convergence. Detailed study-specific evidence is retained in the article cards below.

news.headline_zh: 狂犬病病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期狂犬病病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 已确认巴西政府通过泛美卫生组织向海地公共卫生部捐赠了 10,000 剂人用 狂犬病 疫苗。 [news-abaed3f836051992]
根据第 9482 号共和国法案(2007 年反 狂犬病 法案),确认全市范围内针对流浪狗的“Dakip-Aso”运动,以遏制 狂犬病 案件、咬伤事件和街头事故。 [news-4683bb2b82d1b747]
本文讨论了尼日利亚 狂犬病 的持续威胁,重点关注农牧民冲突及其对公共健康和安全的影响。它不报告任何确诊的 狂犬病 病例或 暴发。 [news-fa18470e9d7542a9]
在人类和动物中确认了 狂犬病 暴发。2026 年上半年,越南在 24 个省/市记录了 39 例人类 狂犬病 死亡和动物 暴发。卫生当局报告,与 2025 年同期相比,狂犬病、受感染动物、动物死亡和扑杀有所增加。数十人在被动物咬伤后需要进行 疫苗接种 接触后治疗。 [news-4bdfe5cb28fd7433]
查塔姆-肯特公共卫生局 (CKPH) 报告称,可预防的野生动物与蝙蝠和浣熊的接触有所增加,导致 狂犬病 暴露后预防 (PEP) 治疗 数量增加。该事件被确认为公共卫生预防通知。 [news-bc22c73ca412b719]
news.trend_or_risk_zh: 风险判断仅依据入选来源已经确认的信息，不把媒体推测升级为官方结论。
news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Rabies virus news developments.
key_findings_en: Confirmed donation of 10,000 doses of human rabies vaccine to Haiti's Ministry of Public Health by the Government of Brazil through PAHO. [news-abaed3f836051992]
Confirmed citywide 'Dakip-Aso' campaign against stray dogs under Republic Act 9482 (Anti-Rabies Act of 2007) to curb rabies cases, bite incidents, and street accidents. [news-4683bb2b82d1b747]

The article discusses the ongoing threat of rabies in Nigeria, focusing on the farmer-herder conflict and its impact on public health and safety. It does not report any confirmed rabies cases or outbreaks. [news-fa18470e9d7542a9]

Confirmed rabies outbreak in humans and animals. Vietnam recorded 39 human rabies deaths and animal outbreaks in 24 provinces/cities in the first half of 2026. Health authorities reported increased outbreaks, infected animals, animal deaths, and culls compared to the same period in 2025. [news-4bdfe5cb28fd7433]

Chatham-Kent Public Health (CKPH) reported an increase in preventable wildlife encounters with bats and raccoons, leading to a rise in Rabies Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) treatments. The event is confirmed as a public health precautionary notice. [news-bc22c73ca412b719]

papers.title: Human Rabies Outbreak in Jaffna District: Is it due to the impact of COVID-19 on rabies control activities?
papers.abstract: Though the number of rabies deaths in Sri Lanka has not changed significantly during/post COVID 19 period, cases in Jaffna has shown a significant increase during this period. This study aimed to determine the possible factors for the increased rabies deaths in the Jaffna District, Sri Lanka.A Desk review was conducted by collecting data of years 2019-2022 from the registers/records maintained in Regional Directorate of Health Services, Jaffna and Medical Officer of Health offices in the Jaffna District. Data was collected using data extraction sheets prepared in Microsoft excel from notification registers, e-mail notifications, special surveillance forms, dog immunization registers/records, dog sterilization registers/records and monthly returns from the hospitals. Triangulation of data was done to ensure data quality. Collected data was analyzed using Microsoft excel functions. Simple descriptive statistics was used to describe the distribution and comparison.Out of 14 rabies death, most of the cases (93%) have occurred among economically active adults and (64%) among males. Distribution of cases was mainly in two land masses, namely Valikamam and Vadamaradchi. MOH Sandilipay had the highest incidence (36%). Proportion of animal bites among OPD attendants varied from 6.9% in 2019 to 11.1% in 2020 and 17.6% in 2021.A reduction was observed in 2022 compared to 2021. Number of dog sterilizations has been fluctuating over the years. Annual dog vaccination coverage in the district varied from 29.3% in 2019 to 86.2% in 2022. In 2019, it varied from 0% in MOH Chankanai, MOH Karainagar, MOH Kayts and MOH Kopay to 105.5% in MOH Chavakacheri. Similarly, in 2022, it varied from 46.3% in MOH Jaffna to 106.6% in MOH Thellipalai. It has observed reduction in human rabies death following increased dog vaccination coverage over the years. There is enough evidence that rabies control activities had been reduced during COVID-19 period and resulted high incidence of animal bites and rabies cases in Jaffna District.

papers.title_original: Human Rabies Outbreak in Jaffna District: Is it due to the impact of COVID-19 on rabies control activities?

analysis.scope_and_question: This review examines the human rabies outbreak in Jaffna District, Sri Lanka, focusing on whether COVID-19 impacted rabies control activities. The central question is to determine factors contributing to increased rabies deaths during the pandemic period.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A desk review was conducted using data from 2019-2022 collected from Regional Directorate of Health Services and Medical Officer of Health offices in Jaffna. Data was extracted from notification registers, email notifications, surveillance forms, dog immunization/sterilization records, and hospital monthly returns using Microsoft Excel. Triangulation ensured data quality, and descriptive statistics were used for analysis.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: There is strong evidence that rabies control activities were reduced during COVID-19, leading to increased animal bites and rabies cases in Jaffna. Increased dog vaccination coverage correlated with reduced human rabies deaths. Most rabies deaths (93%) occurred among economically active adults, with 64% among males, and cases were concentrated in Valikamam and Vadamaradchi regions.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies fluctuations in dog sterilization rates and inconsistent vaccination coverage across Medical Officer of Health areas (ranging from 0% to 106.6%). While the study suggests COVID-19 disrupted rabies control, it does not fully explore other potential contributing factors or long-term impacts beyond 2022.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Priorities include strengthening rabies surveillance systems, improving consistent dog vaccination coverage across all regions, and developing contingency plans for maintaining rabies control during public health emergencies. Enhanced data collection methods and targeted interventions in high-incidence areas like MOH Sandilipay are recommended.

analysis.summary_en: This review investigates the human rabies outbreak in Jaffna District, Sri Lanka, examining the impact of COVID-19 on rabies control activities. Through a desk review of 2019-2022 data, the study found reduced rabies control during the pandemic led to increased animal bites and rabies cases. Key findings include a correlation between higher dog vaccination coverage and reduced human rabies deaths, with most cases affecting economically active males in specific regions. The research highlights inconsistent vaccination coverage across areas and emphasizes the need for strengthened surveillance, consistent dog vaccination programs, and emergency contingency plans to maintain rabies control during future public health crises.

papers.title: Overcoming rabies immune evasion via monoclonal antibody therapeutics.
papers.abstract: Rabies is a lethal acute viral encephalitis caused by neurotropic lyssaviruses, particularly Lyssavirus rabies. The current treatment for rabies exposure involves post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP), which includes the administration of the rabies vaccine and rabies immunoglobulins (RIGs). No effective treatments exist to cure symptomatic rabies. Due to the limited availability and high cost of PEP, tens of thousands of deaths still occur worldwide every year. Monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) represent an effective and economical alternative to RIGs. Moreover, recent preclinical studies have provided evidence that monoclonal antibodies can effectively treat symptomatic rabies, overcoming mechanisms of viral immune evasion. In this review, we critically summarize recent studies, focusing on the treatment of rabies exposures using monoclonal antibodies and the potential of monoclonal antibody-based therapies to combat symptomatic rabies.

papers.title: Safety and operational feasibility of single versus cocktail rabies monoclonal antibodies for post-exposure prophylaxis in a resource-limited setting
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Rabies is almost universally fatal once symptoms develop but is preventable through timely post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP). Global shortages of human and equine rabies immunoglobulin (RIG) have led the World Health Organization to recommend human monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) as acceptable alternatives. Comparative real-world data on single-antibody versus two-antibody cocktail mAbs are limited, particularly from endemic, resource-limited settings. METHODS: A comparative observational study was conducted in a high-volume rabies PEP clinic in India between October 2021 and December 2022. Consecutive patients with category III animal exposures received either a single human anti-rabies mAb (Rabishield; n = 159) or a two-mAb cocktail (Twinrab; n = 159) in combination with WHO-recommended vaccine. Primary outcomes included safety, ease of administration, and operational feasibility. Data were analysed using independent t-tests and chi-square or Fisher's exact tests, with p < 0.05 considered significant. RESULTS: Mean age was 29.7 ± 19.4 years in the Rabishield group and 32.8 ± 20.4 years in the Twinrab group. Ease of infiltration was rated "easy" in 66.7% versus 62.9% of patients (p = 0.63). Local adverse events were uncommon, with pain reported in 2.5% versus 7.5% (p = 0.07) and erythema in ≤ 1.3% of participants. No serious systemic adverse events occurred. Rabishield required more vials per patient (2.28 ± 0.84 vs 2.00 ± 0.69; p = 0.001) and had a higher mean infiltration volume (4.7 ± 1.9 mL vs 4.0 ± 1.6 mL; p < 0.001), while wastage was similar between groups (1.03 ± 0.72 mL vs 1.03 ± 0.69 mL; p = 0.95). CONCLUSIONS: Both single and cocktail human anti-rabies mAbs were safe, well tolerated, and operationally feasible in a programmatic setting. The slightly higher volume and vial requirement for Rabishield may have cost and logistics implications. These findings support broader mAb adoption to address RIG shortages in rabies-endemic, resource-limited settings.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the safety and operational feasibility of single versus cocktail rabies monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) for post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) in a resource-limited setting in India. Rabishield and Twinrab were administered to 159 patients each, with primary outcomes focusing on safety, ease of administration, and operational feasibility. Results showed no serious adverse events, with Rabishield requiring more vials and infiltration volume than Twinrab. The study supports the use of mAbs as alternatives to rabies immunoglobulin (RIG) in areas with shortages, though it does not address long-term efficacy or immune response. The evidence is moderate, as the study is observational and lacks detailed information on the specific mAbs used.

papers.title_zh: 在资源有限的环境中,暴露后预防 单克隆抗体与混合 狂犬病 单克隆抗体的安全性和操作可行性
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Rabies is almost universally fatal once symptoms develop but is preventable through timely post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP). Global shortages of human and equine rabies immunoglobulin (RIG) have led the World Health Organization to recommend human monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) as acceptable alternatives. Comparative real-world data on single-antibody versus two-antibody cocktail mAbs are limited, particularly from endemic, resource-limited settings. METHODS: A comparative observational study was conducted in a high-volume rabies PEP clinic in India between October 2021 and December 2022. Consecutive patients with category III animal exposures received either a single human anti-rabies mAb (Rabishield; n = 159) or a two-mAb cocktail (Twinrab; n = 159) in combination with WHO-recommended vaccine. Primary outcomes included safety, ease of administration, and operational feasibility. Data were analysed using independent t-tests and chi-square or Fisher's exact tests, with p < 0.05 considered significant. RESULTS: Mean age was 29.7 ± 19.4 years in the Rabishield group and 32.8 ± 20.4 years in the Twinrab group. Ease of infiltration was rated "easy" in 66.7% versus 62.9% of patients (p = 0.63). Local adverse events were uncommon, with pain reported in 2.5% versus 7.5% (p = 0.07) and erythema in ≤ 1.3% of participants. No serious systemic adverse events occurred. Rabishield required more vials per patient (2.28 ± 0.84 vs 2.00 ± 0.69; p = 0.001) and had a higher mean infiltration volume (4.7 ± 1.9 mL vs 4.0 ± 1.6 mL; p < 0.001), while wastage was similar between groups (1.03 ± 0.72 mL vs 1.03 ± 0.69 mL; p = 0.95). CONCLUSIONS: Both single and cocktail human anti-rabies mAbs were safe, well tolerated, and operationally feasible in a programmatic setting. The slightly higher volume and vial requirement for Rabishield may have cost and logistics implications. These findings support broader mAb adoption to address RIG shortages in rabies-endemic, resource-limited settings.

papers.title: A Multi-State, Cross-Sectional Retrospective Study on Knowledge, Attitude and Practice of Rabies Post-Exposure Prophylaxis Including Rabies Monoclonal Antibody Among Physicians Across India
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Rabies remains a lethal vaccine-preventable disease in India, and physicians managing animal-bite cases are central to effective post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP). With the increasing use of rabies monoclonal antibodies (RmAbs) as alternatives to conventional rabies immunoglobulins, this study assessed physicians’ knowledge, attitude, and practice (KAP) regarding rabies PEP, including RmAb awareness and acceptance. Methods: This multi-state, cross-sectional retrospective KAP survey was conducted among 208 physicians across ten Indian states using a structured, self-administered Google Form. The 33-item questionnaire assessed Knowledge, Attitude, and Practice domains, with 11 items each, scored binarily according to NCDC guidelines. Descriptive statistics, Shapiro–Wilk normality testing, Kruskal–Wallis tests with post hoc corrections, and Spearman rank-order correlations were performed. Results: Mean domain scores were 8.00/11 for Knowledge (72.7%), 7.22/11 for Attitude (65.6%), and 8.64/11 for Practice (78.5%). Key gaps were identified in the intramuscular pre-exposure prophylaxis schedule, management of excess RIG/RmAb after wound infiltration, exposure categorization of animal contact, and vaccine administration site in young children. The Knowledge–Practice correlation was moderately strong and statistically significant (r = 0.520, p < 0.001). Acceptance of RmAbs was high, with 88.5% recognizing them as effective replacements for RIGs and 84.6% considering them safer than RIGs. Practice scores showed the most consistent improvement, Knowledge scores improved on most items but declined sharply for the pre-exposure prophylaxis schedule, and Attitude scores showed a mixed pattern of gains and losses compared with the 2013 benchmark survey. Conclusions: Overall KAP scores were adequate, with Practice scoring highest. Targeted continuing medical education focused on NCDC guidelines and practical PEP scenarios is needed among physicians managing rabies exposures.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景/目标:狂犬病 在印度仍然是一种致命的 疫苗 可预防疾病,处理动物咬伤病例的医生对于有效 暴露后预防 (PEP) 至关重要。随着越来越多地使用 狂犬病 单克隆抗体 (RmAb) 作为传统 狂犬病 免疫球蛋白的替代品,本研究评估了医生关于 狂犬病 PEP 的知识、态度和实践 (KAP),包括 RmAb 认知和接受度。方法:这项多州、横断面回顾性 KAP 调查是使用结构化、自我管理的 Google 表格对印度 10 个州的 208 名医生进行的。这份包含 33 项的问卷评估了知识、态度和实践领域,每个领域 11 个项目,根据 NCDC 指南进行二进制评分。进行了描述性统计、Shapiro-Wilk 正态性检验、带有事后修正的 Kruskal-Wallis 检验以及 Spearman 排序相关性。结果:知识领域平均得分为 8.00/11 (72.7%),态度领域得分为 7.22/11 (65.6%),实践领域得分为 8.64/11 (78.5%)。在肌内暴露前预防方案、伤口浸润后过量 RIG/RmAb 的管理、动物接触的暴露分类以及幼儿 疫苗 给药部位等方面发现了关键差距。知识与实践的相关性中等强且具有统计显着性(r = 0.520,p < 0.001)。RmAb 的接受度很高,88.5% 的人认为它们是 RIG 的有效替代品,84.6% 的人认为它们比 RIG 更安全。与 2013 年基准调查相比,实践分数显示出最一致的改善,大多数项目的知识分数有所提高,但暴露前预防计划的知识分数急剧下降,态度分数显示出得与失的混合模式。结论:KAP 总体得分足够,其中实践得分最高。管理 狂犬病 暴露的医生需要开展有针对性的继续医学教育,重点关注 NCDC 指南和实际 PEP 场景。

papers.title: Paralytic Rabies Encephalomeningomyelitis: A Tale of Two Cases With Emphasis on Imaging Findings and Relevant Literature Review
papers.abstract: Imaging documentation of rabies encephalitis remains rare because of the progressive and fatal course of the disease. We present two cases of paralytic rabies encephalomeningomyelitis, showing varied imaging findings, one in a two-year-old girl whose magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) illustrated typical features, and another case of a 65-year-old female with atypical MRI findings. These two cases emphasize that classical rabies shows predominant grey-matter involvement, whereas an atypical presentation, particularly in elderly patients with underlying comorbidities, shows a predilection for white matter, in contrast to the typical form. The identification of this varied imaging spectrum is crucial for prompt diagnosis, especially in endemic zones. The rarity of antemortem neuroimaging in rabies, with detailed documentation of typical and atypical cases, enriches the limited diagnostic literature and improves early recognition of the disease’s imaging spectrum.

papers.source_body_en: Imaging documentation of rabies encephalitis remains rare because of the progressive and fatal course of the disease. We present two cases of paralytic rabies encephalomeningomyelitis, showing varied imaging findings, one in a two-year-old girl whose magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) illustrated typical features, and another case of a 65-year-old female with atypical MRI findings. These two cases emphasize that classical rabies shows predominant grey-matter involvement, whereas an atypical presentation, particularly in elderly patients with underlying comorbidities, shows a predilection for white matter, in contrast to the typical form. The identification of this varied imaging spectrum is crucial for prompt diagnosis, especially in endemic zones. The rarity of antemortem neuroimaging in rabies, with detailed documentation of typical and atypical cases, enriches the limited diagnostic literature and improves early recognition of the disease’s imaging spectrum.

papers.title: Transsynaptic neural circuit mapping of ventral hippocampus motivational control systems.
papers.abstract: The ventral hippocampus contributes to food intake regulation and a range of motivational and memory processes, and its dysfunction is associated with several cognitive and behavioral disorders. However, its circuit-level organization remains incompletely understood. Ventral CA1 (CA1v) neurons send projections to several regions involved in motivational control. Here we focus on three major forebrain targets: the nucleus accumbens shell (ACBsh), medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), and lateral hypothalamic area (LHA). We mapped the upstream and downstream circuitry of CA1v neurons defined by their projections to these target regions in rats using complementary transsynaptic anterograde and retrograde viral tracing approaches. Monosynaptic outputs to ACBsh, mPFC, and LHA were targeted using ATLAS, a novel transsynaptic anterograde viral approach that drives Cre recombinase in neurons receiving synaptic transmission from the CA1v. Second-order projections arising from these defined pathways were then mapped using a Cre-dependent anterograde viral tracing strategy. In parallel, upstream inputs to CA1v neurons projecting to each downstream target were mapped using a conditional retrograde glycoprotein-deleted rabies viral approach. Anterograde tracing revealed both shared and pathway-specific second-order targets, including bidirectional CA1v projections. Retrograde tracing confirmed expected inputs (e.g., CA3) and uncovered previously unrecognized cortical sources that differed across downstream projection-defined CA1v subpopulations. Together, these findings delineate pathway-specific, multi-node circuits linking CA1v neurons to key motivational systems that may inform future therapeutic strategies for disorders involving ventral hippocampal dysfunction.

papers.title_zh: 腹侧海马动机控制系统的突触神经回路映射。
papers.source_body_en: The ventral hippocampus contributes to food intake regulation and a range of motivational and memory processes, and its dysfunction is associated with several cognitive and behavioral disorders. However, its circuit-level organization remains incompletely understood. Ventral CA1 (CA1v) neurons send projections to several regions involved in motivational control. Here we focus on three major forebrain targets: the nucleus accumbens shell (ACBsh), medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), and lateral hypothalamic area (LHA). We mapped the upstream and downstream circuitry of CA1v neurons defined by their projections to these target regions in rats using complementary transsynaptic anterograde and retrograde viral tracing approaches. Monosynaptic outputs to ACBsh, mPFC, and LHA were targeted using ATLAS, a novel transsynaptic anterograde viral approach that drives Cre recombinase in neurons receiving synaptic transmission from the CA1v. Second-order projections arising from these defined pathways were then mapped using a Cre-dependent anterograde viral tracing strategy. In parallel, upstream inputs to CA1v neurons projecting to each downstream target were mapped using a conditional retrograde glycoprotein-deleted rabies viral approach. Anterograde tracing revealed both shared and pathway-specific second-order targets, including bidirectional CA1v projections. Retrograde tracing confirmed expected inputs (e.g., CA3) and uncovered previously unrecognized cortical sources that differed across downstream projection-defined CA1v subpopulations. Together, these findings delineate pathway-specific, multi-node circuits linking CA1v neurons to key motivational systems that may inform future therapeutic strategies for disorders involving ventral hippocampal dysfunction.

papers.title: Evaluation of Bait Acceptance and Immune Response in a Local Dog Population During an Oral Rabies Vaccination Field Study in Cambodia
papers.abstract: (1) Background: Dog-mediated human rabies remains a serious public health problem in Cambodia, partially due to the high abundance of dogs. As most dogs are free-roaming and cannot easily be handled and restrained, the rabies vaccination coverage is very low. Oral rabies vaccination (ORV) could increase the vaccination coverage to levels required for interrupting the transmission cycle. (2) Methods: In this study, the bait acceptance and immunogenicity of a commercially available vaccine bait were tested in local free-roaming dogs in the northern part of Takeo province in Cambodia. (3) Results: In total, 75.4% (515/683) of dogs initially showed interest when offered an egg-flavored bait containing the SPBN GASGAS rabies virus vaccine. Subsequently, 89.9% of these dogs consumed the bait, and almost all of them (98.3%) were considered successfully vaccinated. Blood samples were collected from 50 dogs prior to vaccination. Eight of these fifty dogs tested sero-positive for rabies antibodies (ELISA) and were excluded from follow-up samples. Thirty and ninety days post-vaccination, 91.4% and 68.2% of the relocated vaccinated dogs tested sero-positive, respectively. (4) Conclusions: Bait acceptance and immunogenicity showed similar results as observed in studies with the same vaccine bait conducted in other countries. Hence, ORV seems to be a very promising tool for dog rabies control in Cambodia, which has a large owned but free-roaming dog population.

papers.title: Rabies Despite Postexposure Prophylaxis in High-Burden Settings: Vaccine Failure or Gaps in Healthcare Delivery?
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Rabies, a fatal zoonotic encephalitis, is preventable through timely postexposure prophylaxis (PEP), which includes wound care, vaccination, and local infiltration of immunoglobulins. However, reports of rabies despite PEP raise concerns about vaccine efficacy and protocol adherence. This study aimed to assess the burden and underlying causes of such apparent rabies "breakthrough" infections. METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed laboratory-confirmed rabies cases from 2018 to 2024 who had received PEP. Cases with at least 1 documented dose of rabies vaccine were included. "True" breakthrough infections (or PEP failures) were defined as rabies occurring despite initiation of PEP within 2 calendar days of exposure and documented completion of all required PEP components. RESULTS: Eighty-nine cases fulfilling the inclusion criteria were analyzed; only 3 were classified as "true" breakthrough infections. A majority of the cases were males (80.90%), and aged less than 15 years (64.04%). Exposure to dogs was reported in 93.26% cases, 80.9% were World Health Organization (WHO) Category III exposures, and 34.83% involved the head or neck. Postexposure prophylaxis was initiated within 2 days in 57.3% of cases; wound care was documented in 56.18%, vaccination completed in 46.07%, and only 26.39% of Category III cases received rabies immunoglobulins without any deviations. CONCLUSIONS: The findings indicate that "true" breakthrough infections are uncommon, with most apparent PEP failures resulting from gaps in healthcare delivery. Such failures can undermine public confidence in vaccination, highlighting the need to strengthen awareness among healthcare workers and communities about the critical steps of PEP.

The research analyzed laboratory-confirmed rabies cases from 2018 to 2024 who had received PEP, with inclusion criteria requiring at least one documented dose of rabies vaccine. Only 3 out of 89 analyzed cases were classified as "true" breakthrough infections, indicating that most cases of rabies following PEP were due to gaps in healthcare delivery rather than vaccine failure. The evidence suggests that while the study provides valuable insights into PEP effectiveness, it does not explicitly report limitations or evidence strength assessment.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 狂犬病 是一种致命的人畜共患脑炎,可以通过及时的暴露后预防 (PEP) 来预防,其中包括伤口护理、狂犬病 和免疫球蛋白的局部浸润。然而,尽管 PEP 的 狂犬病 报告仍引发了人们对 疫苗 功效和方案遵守情况的担忧。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项回顾性研究分析了 2018 年至 2024 年接受暴露后预防的实验室确诊 狂犬病 病例。包括至少 1 次 狂犬病 疫苗 剂量记录的病例。
elements_zh.methods: 这项研究旨在评估这种明显的 狂犬病“突破性”感染的负担和根本原因。“真正的”突破性感染(或 PEP 失败)被定义为 狂犬病,尽管在暴露后 2 个日历日内启动了 PEP,并且记录了所有必需 PEP 组件的完成情况,但仍发生了 狂犬病。
elements_zh.main_results: 对符合纳入标准的 89 例病例进行了分析;只有 3 例被归类为“真正的”突破性感染。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,“真正的”突破性感染并不常见,最明显的 PEP 失败是由于医疗服务提供方面的差距造成的。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 此类失败可能会削弱公众对 疫苗接种 的信心,突显出需要加强医护人员和社区对 PEP 关键步骤的认识。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告研究设计或证据强度评估的具体局限性。

papers.title_zh: 狂犬病 尽管在高负担环境中进行暴露后预防:疫苗 医疗服务中的失败或差距?
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Rabies, a fatal zoonotic encephalitis, is preventable through timely postexposure prophylaxis (PEP), which includes wound care, vaccination, and local infiltration of immunoglobulins. However, reports of rabies despite PEP raise concerns about vaccine efficacy and protocol adherence. This study aimed to assess the burden and underlying causes of such apparent rabies "breakthrough" infections. METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed laboratory-confirmed rabies cases from 2018 to 2024 who had received PEP. Cases with at least 1 documented dose of rabies vaccine were included. "True" breakthrough infections (or PEP failures) were defined as rabies occurring despite initiation of PEP within 2 calendar days of exposure and documented completion of all required PEP components. RESULTS: Eighty-nine cases fulfilling the inclusion criteria were analyzed; only 3 were classified as "true" breakthrough infections. A majority of the cases were males (80.90%), and aged less than 15 years (64.04%). Exposure to dogs was reported in 93.26% cases, 80.9% were World Health Organization (WHO) Category III exposures, and 34.83% involved the head or neck. Postexposure prophylaxis was initiated within 2 days in 57.3% of cases; wound care was documented in 56.18%, vaccination completed in 46.07%, and only 26.39% of Category III cases received rabies immunoglobulins without any deviations. CONCLUSIONS: The findings indicate that "true" breakthrough infections are uncommon, with most apparent PEP failures resulting from gaps in healthcare delivery. Such failures can undermine public confidence in vaccination, highlighting the need to strengthen awareness among healthcare workers and communities about the critical steps of PEP.

papers.title: Rabies-related knowledge, attitudes, and practices among dog owners in Lawra and Jirapa Municipalities, Upper West Region, Ghana
papers.abstract: Introduction: Rabies is a neglected zoonotic disease affecting poor and remote human settlements disproportionately relative to urban rich communities. In rural areas, rabies cases often go unreported, as awareness of the disease is low and surveillance is sub-optimal. An understanding of dog ecology has been recognised as a key factor in designing an effective rabies control program in rabies-endemic countries. This study assessed the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) of rabies control among dog owners in Lawra and Jirapa Municipalities in the Upper West Region of Ghana. Methods: A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among 370 dog owners aged 18 and above, selected through multistage sampling. Data were collected using structured questionnaires and analysed using descriptive and inferential statistics in Stata 17.0. Composite scores were generated to quantify rabies knowledge, attitudes toward anti-rabies vaccination, dog-bite-related practices, and rabies control measures. As part of the study, dogs in participating households were vaccinated against rabies free of charge. Results: Rabies awareness was high in both municipalities, with Jirapa at 97.6% and Lawra at 77.0%. Vaccination-related practices scored highly across the 10 assessed domains. Dog bite prevalence was notably higher in Jirapa (44.1%) than in Lawra (20.5%). While most bite victims in Lawra visited health facilities, 38.4% in Jirapa relied on traditional remedies. Associations were found between demographic factors and rabies-related KAP. Conclusion: The study recommends collaborative engagement of local health authorities, community leaders, and media to translate the high rabies awareness and positive vaccination attitudes into strengthening preventive practices, particularly appropriate responses following dog bites, in both municipalities.
papers.journal: Journal of Interventional Epidemiology and Public Health

papers.title_zh: 加纳上西区劳拉市和吉拉帕市养狗者的 狂犬病 相关知识、态度和做法
papers.source_body_en: Introduction: Rabies is a neglected zoonotic disease affecting poor and remote human settlements disproportionately relative to urban rich communities. In rural areas, rabies cases often go unreported, as awareness of the disease is low and surveillance is sub-optimal. An understanding of dog ecology has been recognised as a key factor in designing an effective rabies control program in rabies-endemic countries. This study assessed the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) of rabies control among dog owners in Lawra and Jirapa Municipalities in the Upper West Region of Ghana. Methods: A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among 370 dog owners aged 18 and above, selected through multistage sampling. Data were collected using structured questionnaires and analysed using descriptive and inferential statistics in Stata 17.0. Composite scores were generated to quantify rabies knowledge, attitudes toward anti-rabies vaccination, dog-bite-related practices, and rabies control measures. As part of the study, dogs in participating households were vaccinated against rabies free of charge. Results: Rabies awareness was high in both municipalities, with Jirapa at 97.6% and Lawra at 77.0%. Vaccination-related practices scored highly across the 10 assessed domains. Dog bite prevalence was notably higher in Jirapa (44.1%) than in Lawra (20.5%). While most bite victims in Lawra visited health facilities, 38.4% in Jirapa relied on traditional remedies. Associations were found between demographic factors and rabies-related KAP. Conclusion: The study recommends collaborative engagement of local health authorities, community leaders, and media to translate the high rabies awareness and positive vaccination attitudes into strengthening preventive practices, particularly appropriate responses following dog bites, in both municipalities.

papers.title: Exploring Zoonotic Disease Knowledge Through AI for Enhanced Risk, Prevention, and Response Awareness in Low-Resource Languages
papers.abstract: Limited linguistic inclusivity in public health communication leaves many South African communities underserved, particularly regarding critical information on zoonotic diseases such as rabies. This pilot study addresses this gap by developing and evaluating AI-driven methods for delivering reliable rabies information to Sepedi speakers, a low-resource language group. The study presents a novel, curated Sepedi dataset of 60 question–answer pairs, created through a systematic pipeline: thematic analysis of authoritative English sources guided the synthetic generation of QA pairs, which were then translated and manually verified by a native-speaking expert. This dataset was used to compare two large language models, GPT-4o and Gemini-1.5 Flash, under both base and fine-tuned conditions. Evaluation used a human-centred rubric assessing fluency, accuracy, and cultural appropriateness. The findings reveal a key nuance in applying LLMs to low-resource domains. The base GPT-4o model, with strong foundational multilingual capabilities, outperformed all other configurations, including its own fine-tuned variant.In contrast, fine-tuning provided a marked improvement for the less capable base Gemini model. This result indicates that fine-tuning can enhance weaker models; its benefits are not universal and may be outweighed by the strong zero-shot performance of state-of-the-art architectures when training data is scarce. The curated Sepedi rabies QA dataset will be released under an open licence to support future work in low-resource public health communication.

papers.title_zh: 通过人工智能探索人畜共患疾病知识,以增强低资源语言的风险、预防和应对意识
papers.source_body_en: Limited linguistic inclusivity in public health communication leaves many South African communities underserved, particularly regarding critical information on zoonotic diseases such as rabies. This pilot study addresses this gap by developing and evaluating AI-driven methods for delivering reliable rabies information to Sepedi speakers, a low-resource language group. The study presents a novel, curated Sepedi dataset of 60 question–answer pairs, created through a systematic pipeline: thematic analysis of authoritative English sources guided the synthetic generation of QA pairs, which were then translated and manually verified by a native-speaking expert. This dataset was used to compare two large language models, GPT-4o and Gemini-1.5 Flash, under both base and fine-tuned conditions. Evaluation used a human-centred rubric assessing fluency, accuracy, and cultural appropriateness. The findings reveal a key nuance in applying LLMs to low-resource domains. The base GPT-4o model, with strong foundational multilingual capabilities, outperformed all other configurations, including its own fine-tuned variant.In contrast, fine-tuning provided a marked improvement for the less capable base Gemini model. This result indicates that fine-tuning can enhance weaker models; its benefits are not universal and may be outweighed by the strong zero-shot performance of state-of-the-art architectures when training data is scarce. The curated Sepedi rabies QA dataset will be released under an open licence to support future work in low-resource public health communication.

papers.title: Transsynaptic viral tools in neural circuit analysis: from anatomical mapping to functional interrogation
papers.abstract: The application of transsynaptic viruses has transformed neural circuit analysis, enabling increasingly precise mapping of neuronal connectivity. These approaches can be broadly divided into polysynaptic and monosynaptic strategies. Polysynaptic retrograde tracers based on pseudorabies virus, including the classically selected Bartha strain and genetically engineered retrograde variants have provided important insights into multisynaptic circuit organization in rodents. For polysynaptic anterograde tracing, herpes simplex virus strain H129 and its derivatives have been used to map output pathways, with later genetic modifications improving detectability and experimental control. Over the past few years, growing attention has shifted toward monosynaptic tracing based on engineered rabies virus platforms used in combination with adeno-associated virus helper systems, which enable genetically restricted spread to direct presynaptic partners. Viral tracing is increasingly integrated with functional approaches, including calcium and voltage imaging, optogenetics, chemogenetics, and recombinase-based genetic strategies, thereby extending circuit analysis from anatomical mapping to causal interrogation of the function of defined neuronal populations. Looking forward, improved control of polysynaptic spread, together with large transgene capacity, suitability for tracing hierarchical circuit architecture, and the ability to incorporate functional readouts, is expected to revive interest in multisynaptic tracing.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the transformation of neural circuit analysis through transsynaptic viral tools, focusing on their evolution from anatomical mapping to functional interrogation of neuronal connectivity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The review broadly categorizes transsynaptic viral approaches into polysynaptic and monosynaptic strategies, examining their applications in rodents and integration with functional methods.
analysis.methods: The analysis evaluates viral tracing techniques including pseudorabies virus-based retrograde tracers, herpes simplex virus anterograde tracing, and engineered rabies virus platforms combined with adeno-associated virus helper systems for monosynaptic tracing.
analysis.main_results: Polysynaptic retrograde tracers like Bartha strain pseudorabies virus and genetically engineered variants have provided insights into multisynaptic circuit organization, while herpes simplex virus H129 derivatives have been used for anterograde mapping with improved detectability.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that viral tracing has evolved from anatomical mapping to functional interrogation through integration with calcium imaging, optogenetics, chemogenetics, and genetic strategies, enabling causal analysis of neuronal populations.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform future neural circuit research by demonstrating how viral tools can be combined with functional approaches to understand circuit architecture and function, potentially advancing therapeutic interventions for neurological disorders.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate as this is a review article summarizing existing techniques rather than presenting new primary data, with limitations including the need for improved control of polysynaptic spread and large transgene capacity for multisynaptic tracing.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines how transsynaptic viral tools have transformed neural circuit analysis, dividing approaches into polysynaptic and monosynaptic strategies. Polysynaptic retrograde tracers like pseudorabies virus have mapped multisynaptic circuits in rodents, while herpes simplex virus derivatives enable anterograde tracing. Engineered rabies virus platforms with adeno-associated virus helpers allow monosynaptic tracing to direct presynaptic partners. The integration of viral tracing with functional methods like calcium imaging, optogenetics, and chemogenetics extends analysis from anatomical mapping to functional interrogation. Future improvements in controlling polysynaptic spread and incorporating functional readouts are expected to advance multisynaptic tracing capabilities.

elements_zh.methods: 该分析评估了病毒追踪技术,包括基于伪狂犬病病毒的逆行追踪、单纯疱疹病毒顺行追踪,以及与腺相关病毒辅助系统相结合的工程化 狂犬病病毒 平台,用于单突触追踪。
elements_zh.main_results: 多突触逆行示踪剂(如 Bartha 株伪狂犬病病毒和基因工程变体)为多突触回路组织提供了见解,而单纯疱疹病毒 H129 衍生物已用于顺行作图,并提高了可检测性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,通过与钙成像、光遗传学、化学遗传学和遗传策略的整合,病毒追踪已经从解剖图谱发展到功能询问,从而能够对神经元群体进行因果分析。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现通过展示病毒工具如何与功能方法相结合来了解神经回路的架构和功能,为未来的神经回路研究提供信息,从而有可能推进神经系统疾病的治疗干预。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据强度中等,因为这是一篇总结现有技术的评论文章,而不是提供新的原始数据,其局限性包括需要改进对多突触扩散的控制和多突触追踪的大转基因能力。

papers.title: Traveling waves of a reaction-diffusion system with partially coupled diffusion
papers.abstract: This work is devoted to the study of traveling wave solutions of reaction-diffusion systems, where the diffusion rate of~$v$, the second component, depends on~$u$, the first component. Such systems arise in prey-predator models, where the predator~$v$ is actively hunting its prey~$u$, or in epidemiological models where the disease induces erratic behavior, for example rabies. This results in a quasilinear coupling in the highest-order term of the equation for~$v$. From the theoretical point of view, we fully classify traveling wave solutions when the first component does not diffuse, in which case the problem can be reduced to a nonlinear scalar equation. The case where both components diffuse is investigated numerically.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to classify traveling wave solutions in reaction-diffusion systems where diffusion rates are partially coupled, with applications to epidemiological models like rabies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research focused on theoretical classification and numerical investigation of traveling wave solutions in reaction-diffusion systems, particularly when the first component does not diffuse.
analysis.methods: Theoretical analysis reduced the problem to a nonlinear scalar equation when the first component does not diffuse, while numerical methods were used for cases where both components diffuse.
analysis.main_results: Traveling wave solutions were fully classified when the first component does not diffuse, and the case where both components diffuse was investigated numerically.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as a theoretical advancement in understanding traveling wave solutions in partially coupled systems, with novelty in the classification of solutions under specific diffusion conditions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform mathematical modeling of disease spread, particularly for rabies, where erratic behavior affects diffusion rates, aiding in epidemic prediction and control strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on theoretical and numerical approaches without empirical validation, and the study's scope is limited to specific diffusion scenarios.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates traveling wave solutions in reaction-diffusion systems with partially coupled diffusion, focusing on cases where the diffusion rate of one component depends on another. Theoretical classification was achieved when the first component does not diffuse, reducing the problem to a nonlinear scalar equation, while numerical methods explored cases where both components diffuse. The research has applications in epidemiological models like rabies, where disease-induced erratic behavior affects diffusion rates. The findings advance mathematical understanding of disease spread dynamics, though the evidence strength is moderate due to the lack of empirical validation.

Haiti - Maritime Scholarships : Call for Applications Haiti - Security : The United States lifts restrictions that limited its cooperation with the FAd'H Haiti - Moscow : Haitian student Slanda François, detained in Russia, released Zapping Haiti of July 24, 2026 more news Donation from Brazil of 10,000 doses of human rabies vaccine Haiti's PM pays tribute to the great figures of Konpa FLASH : Medinel Zamor injured, out of the U-20 Champions League Championship Colombia : Haiti's Mission on cocoa Venezuela : Haiti honors its medical brigade returning from its solidarity mission more news Donation from Brazil of 10,000 doses of human rabies vaccine 25/07/2026 11:02:52 On Thursday, July 22, 2026, the Ministry of Public Health received a donation of 10,000 doses of human rabies vaccine at the PROMESS warehouse. The donation was provided by the Government of Brazil through the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO). The delivery of this significant donation to Haiti was made possible through the joint efforts of PANAFTOSA, the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), and the logistical support of the World Food Programme (WFP), which facilitated the air transport of the vaccines to Port-au-Prince. This donation comes at a time when rabies remains a public health threat in Haiti. Between the first and twenty-fourth epidemiological weeks of 2026, 1,481 attacks by animals suspected of having rabies were reported in the country, including 3 deaths, with the situation remaining concentrated in the Central and Western departments. Although this disease is preventable with prompt treatment after exposure, it is almost always fatal once symptoms appear. Access to rabies vaccines is therefore essential to protect populations exposed to animal bites. Thanks to this contribution from the Brazilian Government, health authorities will have a strengthened stockpile, enabling them to improve the care of people exposed to rabies and support prevention efforts in several departments of the country. This initiative illustrates the importance of regional solidarity and coordinated international cooperation in addressing health challenges. It is part of the ongoing efforts of the Ministry of Public Health and Population (MSPP), with the support of friendly countries like Brazil and the United States, and its partners like the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), to reduce the risk of rabies-related deaths and ensure better access to essential health products. This donation arrives amid a concerning rabies situation in Haiti, where 1,481 suspected animal attacks and 3 deaths were reported in the first 24 weeks of 2026, primarily in the Central and Western departments. The vaccines will bolster Haiti's stockpile, enabling better post-exposure treatment and prevention efforts. news.content: SectionsNews Watch Live Local News National News Politics Entertainment News Watch Live Sports Bahakel Sports Local Sports National Sports USC Gamecocks Clemson Gamecock Saturday Night High School Football –Friday Night Fever Weather Today’s Forecast Radar Weather Photo of the Week Weather Blog Programming ABC DABL Heroes & Icons MeTV MeTV Toons Start TV TV Schedule Children’s Programming Mugshots SecondaryTraffic Contests Tyler’s Travels, Love it or Chuck it Midlands Cares Midlands Military Matters Midlands Pup Shots America 250 WOLOMeTV About Us Contact Us Local Events ABC Columbia Search MeTV About Us Contact Us Local Events News Watch Live Local News National News Politics Entertainment News Watch Live Sports Bahakel Sports Local Sports National Sports USC Gamecocks Clemson Gamecock Saturday Night High School Football –Friday Night Fever Weather Today’s Forecast Radar Weather Photo of the Week Weather Blog Programming ABC DABL Heroes & Icons MeTV MeTV Toons Start TV TV Schedule Children’s Programming Mugshots Traffic Contests Tyler’s Travels, Love it or Chuck it Midlands Cares Midlands Military Matters Midlands Pup Shots America 250 Rabies — how to protect your pets and loved ones from the virus Jul 21, 2026 5:50 PM EDT Lee Williams, COLUMBIA, SC (WOLO) — Health officials with the South Carolina Department of Public Health confirmed three cases of rabies -two rabid racoons and one rabid bat across Charleston, York, and Saluda Counties. All are being treated or quarantined according to health guidelines. So how is rabies contracted? Health officials say the virus can be transmitted through contact with an infected animal’s saliva, such as from a bite or scratch. According to the CDC, animals most frequently found with rabies in the U.S. are bats, skunks, raccoons, and foxes. Around 100,000 people across the U.S. are vaccinated against the virus following a potential rabies exposure each year. DPH’s Rabies Program Manager, Terri McCollister, says there are ways to try and steer clear from the virus. First — never handle a bat or any wild or stray animal with your bare hands, whether it’s dead or alive. When it comes to bats, McCollister says people don’t always realize that they, or a pet, have been bitten — since the animal’s teeth are so tiny — making bites easy to overlook. Because of this, you should always assume a person, or pet, has potentially been bitten should you wake up to find a bat in, say, a bedroom or tent — or a bat is found where children, pets, or mentally impaired people have been left unattended. According to McCollister, a bat that is active by day, found where bats are not usually seen, or is unable to fly is far more likely to be rabid. However, there is no guarantee that a rabid bat will behave any differently than a healthy bat. If you think you may have been exposed to an animal with rabies, immediately wash the affected area with plenty of soap and water, and seek medical attention to determine whether any follow‐up care is needed. If you choose not to seek medical care, contact your county office to report the incident so they can try and track down the animal. To help protect pets, McCollister says keep them up-to-date on their rabies vaccination — which remains one of the most effective defenses. DPH reports 62 cases of rabid animals so far this year. On average, about 136 are reported annually. McCollister also says it is a normal trend to see increased positive cases of rabies in South Carolina between the months of August and October. The exact reason for this isn’t known, but there are several human and animal behavior factors that might be involved. Other southeastern states have similar trends. If you believe you, someone you know, or a pet has been exposed, you can call DPH’s 24-hour rabies reporting line at (888) 847-0902 (select option 2). You can also find additional reporting information on DPH’s website here. For a list of wildlife animal removal services, click here. news.content: Quảng cáo của DTadsSunday, 26 July 2026Tiếng ViệtRSSVIETNAM TODAYBusinessSocietyEducationEnvironmentLIFESTYLETravelEntertainmentFood & DrinkCULTURE AND SPORTCultureSportCOMMUNITYMULTI MEDIACopiedVIETNAM TODAYVietnam records 39 rabies deaths in first half of 2026July 24, 2026 - 08:21 PMVietnam recorded 39 rabies deaths across 18 provinces and cities in the first six months of 2026, while outbreaks among animals continued to rise, health authorities said.said.Vaccinating dogs and cats against rabies helps reduce the risk of transmission to humans (Illustrative photo: Shutterstock).Vietnam recorded 39 deaths from rabies across 18 provinces and cities in the first half of 2026, according to the Ministry of Health.The ministry said southern Vietnam accounted for 20 deaths, while 10 were recorded in the north and nine in the central and Central Highlands regions.During the same period, rabies outbreaks in animals were reported in 24 provinces and cities. Compared with the first half of 2025, the number of outbreaks, infected animals, animal deaths and culls all increased.Nguyen Dinh Dang, head of the Hanoi Department of Livestock Production, Fisheries and Animal Health, said the capital had recorded eight animal rabies outbreaks in six communes since the beginning of the year. Dozens of people required post-exposure vaccination after being bitten by animals suspected of carrying the virus.Dang said rabies remained one of the country's most dangerous infectious diseases, posing risks throughout the breeding, transport, slaughter and trade of dogs and cats."Controlling vaccination, regulating the transport, slaughter and trade of dogs and cats, while avoiding the slaughter and consumption of dog and cat meat, may seem like small measures, but they are essential to eliminating rabies and preventing further deaths," Dang said.Hanoi is home to nearly 360,000 dogs and cats, he said, adding that managing pets, animal transport and slaughter remained a major challenge. According to official data, all recorded rabies outbreaks in animals have originated in dogs.The capital has not recorded a human rabies death since 2023, although the disease continues to circulate among animals.According to the Hanoi Centre for Disease Control, around 5,000 people seek medical consultation and preventive rabies treatment each month.Meanwhile, Ho Chi Minh City recorded five rabies deaths in the first six months of the year. Health authorities said none of the victims had received rabies vaccination or rabies immunoglobulin after being bitten by dogs or cats.Health experts stressed that rabies is almost invariably fatal once symptoms develop. news.content_original: Quảng cáo của DTadsSunday, 26 July 2026Tiếng ViệtRSSVIETNAM TODAYBusinessSocietyEducationEnvironmentLIFESTYLETravelEntertainmentFood & DrinkCULTURE AND SPORTCultureSportCOMMUNITYMULTI MEDIACopiedVIETNAM TODAYVietnam records 39 rabies deaths in first half of 2026July 24, 2026 - 08:21 PMVietnam recorded 39 rabies deaths across 18 provinces and cities in the first six months of 2026, while outbreaks among animals continued to rise, health authorities said.said.Vaccinating dogs and cats against rabies helps reduce the risk of transmission to humans (Illustrative photo: Shutterstock).Vietnam recorded 39 deaths from rabies across 18 provinces and cities in the first half of 2026, according to the Ministry of Health.The ministry said southern Vietnam accounted for 20 deaths, while 10 were recorded in the north and nine in the central and Central Highlands regions.During the same period, rabies outbreaks in animals were reported in 24 provinces and cities. Compared with the first half of 2025, the number of outbreaks, infected animals, animal deaths and culls all increased.Nguyen Dinh Dang, head of the Hanoi Department of Livestock Production, Fisheries and Animal Health, said the capital had recorded eight animal rabies outbreaks in six communes since the beginning of the year. Dozens of people required post-exposure vaccination after being bitten by animals suspected of carrying the virus.Dang said rabies remained one of the country's most dangerous infectious diseases, posing risks throughout the breeding, transport, slaughter and trade of dogs and cats."Controlling vaccination, regulating the transport, slaughter and trade of dogs and cats, while avoiding the slaughter and consumption of dog and cat meat, may seem like small measures, but they are essential to eliminating rabies and preventing further deaths," Dang said.Hanoi is home to nearly 360,000 dogs and cats, he said, adding that managing pets, animal transport and slaughter remained a major challenge. According to official data, all recorded rabies outbreaks in animals have originated in dogs.The capital has not recorded a human rabies death since 2023, although the disease continues to circulate among animals.According to the Hanoi Centre for Disease Control, around 5,000 people seek medical consultation and preventive rabies treatment each month.Meanwhile, Ho Chi Minh City recorded five rabies deaths in the first six months of the year. Health authorities said none of the victims had received rabies vaccination or rabies immunoglobulin after being bitten by dogs or cats.Health experts stressed that rabies is almost invariably fatal once symptoms develop. However, they said the disease is entirely preventable through immediate wound care and timely post-exposure vaccination.Source: dantri.com.vnQuảng cáo của DTadsMore newsQuang Ninh to launch electric analysis.time: Publication date: 2026-07-24. Event period: First half of 2026 (January-June 2026).
analysis.location_and_population: Affected regions: 18 provinces and cities (20 deaths in the south, 10 in the north, 9 in central and Central Highlands regions). Specific locations: Hanoi (8 animal outbreaks in 6 communes), Ho Chi Minh City (5 human deaths). Affected population: Humans (39 deaths) and animals (outbreaks in 24 provinces/cities).
analysis.event: Confirmed rabies outbreak in humans and animals. Vietnam recorded 39 human rabies deaths and animal outbreaks in 24 provinces/cities in the first half of 2026. Health authorities reported increased outbreaks, infected animals, animal deaths, and culls compared to the same period in 2025. Dozens of people required post-exposure vaccination after animal bites.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Human cases: 39 deaths (20 south, 10 north, 9 central/Central Highlands). Animal outbreaks: 24 provinces/cities. Hanoi: 8 animal outbreaks, ~5,000 monthly consultations for rabies treatment. Ho Chi Minh City: 5 human deaths. Risk: Rabies described as one of Vietnam's most dangerous infectious diseases, with ongoing circulation among animals. All animal outbreaks originated in dogs. Risk factors include unvaccinated populations and exposure to dog/cat meat trade.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Response: Health authorities monitoring outbreaks; Hanoi managing ~360,000 dogs/cats. Challenges include regulating animal transport, slaughter, and trade. Prevention measures: Vaccination of dogs/cats, wound care, post-exposure vaccination. Uncertainties: None of the 39 victims received vaccination or immunoglobulin after bites; Hanoi has not recorded a human death since 2023 despite animal circulation. Disease status: Rabies is almost invariably fatal once symptoms develop but entirely preventable with timely intervention.

analysis.brief_en: Vietnam reported 39 rabies deaths across 18 provinces and cities in the first half of 2026, with southern regions accounting for 20 fatalities. Animal outbreaks increased compared to 2025, affecting 24 provinces, primarily originating in dogs. Hanoi recorded 8 animal outbreaks in 6 communes, while Ho Chi Minh City reported 5 human deaths. Health authorities highlighted the disease's severity, noting none of the victims received post-exposure prophylaxis. Despite challenges in managing over 360,000 dogs and cats in Hanoi, officials emphasized vaccination and regulation of animal trade as critical to eliminating rabies. The disease remains preventable through prompt wound care and vaccination but is almost invariably fatal once symptoms appear.

news.content: 🏠 About Us Submit News Newsletter Donate Subscribe Find a Paper News Crime Running Commentary Local Business Community Politics e-Edition Obituaries Opinion Sports Behind the Bench Special Sections Best Of 2022 Magazine 2023 Magazine 2024 Magazine 2025 Magazine Best of Contest Classifieds Jobs Real Estate Autos Legals 🏆 Remarkable Women Cutest Creatures $5,000 Sweepstakes e-Edition State warns pet owners to vaccinate for rabies Bats are common throughout Nevada, with their activity increasing between May and October. Nevada Department of Agriculture photo Staff Reports Thursday, July 23, 2026 Share this: Email | Facebook | X Rabies has been detected in bats captured in Lyon, White Pine and Clark counties that tested positive for rabies prompting a reminder from the Nevada Department of Agriculture for residents to protect themselves and their pets.“Rabies can be effectively controlled with proper vaccination,” said NDA State Veterinarian Dr. Peter Rolfe, DVM. “Keeping pets up to date on vaccines is the best way to protect both animals and the people around them.”The Department’s Animal Disease Laboratory confirms rabies in multiple bats from across the state every year, highlighting the importance of vaccination and vigilance. Since the beginning of the year, the laboratory has identified three bats from Lyon, White Pine and Clark counties that tested positive for rabies.Rabies is a deadly virus that can affect mammals, including dogs, cats, livestock and humans. In Nevada, bats are active from May through October and can enter homes or barns undetected. While bats are the most common source of transmission in the state, other wildlife can also carry the virus.“Annual monitoring in Nevada continues to identify bats that test positive for rabies, reinforcing the need for preventive care,” Animal Disease Laboratory supervisor added Laura Morrow,. “Testing helps us track where the virus is present and provide information to the public and animal health agencies, supporting their response to potential exposures.” Nevada law requires dogs, cats and ferrets to be vaccinated against rabies. Vaccines are also available for certain livestock species. Animal owners should work with their veterinarians to maintain an appropriate vaccination schedule.“Maintaining current rabies vaccinations for pets and avoiding direct contact with wildlife are critical steps in reducing risk,” said NDA Director J.J. Goicoechea. “Bats, in particular, should never be handled, as they can carry rabies even when no obvious signs of illness are present.”For more information on rabies prevention, visit the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention website at cdc.gov/rabies or contact the Southern Nevada Health District, Northern Nevada Public Health or your local veterinarian.Anyone who encounters a bat or other wildlife that may have rabies should contact their local animal control office, vector control or health department for assistance. Do not attempt to pick up the bat without guidance. Suspected rabies exposure or cases in animals should be reported to the NDA Animal Disease Laboratory at diseasereporting@agri.nv.gov or (775) 353-3709. I woke up before dawn on the 4th of July and went out...Of course it happened on a holiday. I woke up before dawn on the 4th of July and went out to tidy my porch, and picked up a live bat, I mistook for a leaf on my wicker sofa. I let go of him fast but the potential horror and the painful suspense and treatment is ongoing. It turns out touching a bat is regarded by the Ulster County Department of Health is as dangerous as being bitten by one. Bats drool. And if rabid, their saliva carries the rabies virus. And if infected, almost no one survives rabies. There are recent news accounts of children dying after accidental contact with bats. One boy in Canada awoke with a bat spread out over his nose and mouth. He didn’t seem to be bitten, but he died. It turns out “contact” may be elusive to diagnose – bats have tiny teeth and you might not feel you were bitten. But as I’ve learned to my horror, you don’t have to be bitten at all – the mere contact can be deadly, as bats drool, and their saliva, if they are rabid, carries the lethal rabies virus. At first, my accidental contact didn’t seem that alarming. I’ve lived happily with the bats behind my shutters for 45 years as they would flutter out at dusk and eat thousands of mosquitoes...I knew they were there as they also left huge black piles of guano, which I swept off my porch onto my rose garden where it was excellent fertilizer. I would occasionally hear their faint chirps behind the shutters, and once my husband was hosing the clapboard above the shutters, and they flew out below his underarms and he didn’t know, but I watched the black cloud flee... Several years ago, I actually worried about the bats when they seemed to have disappeared during a known outbreak of “white nose” disease which was killing bats en masse. There were many articles and notices that we needed those bats to recover and survive, as they are important in the environmental chain of command. People were advised to install bat houses to help them out. My area, Marbletown-Rosendale, is famous for its huge cavern hibernaculum (cave where bats hibernate, forbidden for humans to enter during their winter hibernation period), the Walter Williams Preserve (also known as the "Rosendale Bat Cave"), an abandoned, former limestone cement mine that now serves as a designated winter habitat for federally protected endangered bats, including the Indiana bat. It was there in 2007-8, that the fungus infection White-nose syndrome (WNS) is a deadly fungal disease that devastated bat populations across the Northeast was first reported. Ulster County holds historical significance as one of the primary epicenters of the disease. Caused by the fungus Pseudogymnoascus destructans (Pd), it thrives in the cold, damp environments of caves and abandoned mines. Most of the bats died. So for several summers, I actually missed my bats and was sad when only a few tiny guano droppings would appear, but this year they seemed back to normal. For my own situation of having I thought a casual insignificant contact with a bat,, I checked online and read one post that stated the notorious intramuscular series of vaccinations shots were now down to a routine two regular injections, but now I know to my regret that is incorrect. I waited two days to go down to Ellenville ER and request the vaccinations, only to discover Ellenville doesn’t stock the vaccine, even though demand is high. The Ellenville nurses took down my information and filled out a Department of Health form, stressed that this had to be reported to the Ulster County Department of Health, and I’d best get the shots, asap! In our neck of the woods, the only hospital to give the shots is HealthAlliance in Kingston. The vaccinations must be administered where you have had the bite or contact, in Ulster County, so no dashing across the river. Ellenville and the urgent care offices send everyone to Kingston, where the HealthAlliance staff is not too happy about all the referrals....and Ulster hospital ER means long waits. At HealthAlliance they had to phone the Department of Health for a Human Rabies Authorization for RPEP, Human Rabies Postexposure Prophylaxis. As by then it was one a.m., I asked “won’t they be out or asleep? “We wake them up,” was the answer.Whoever the nurse reached, even at 1 a.m., approved me and right now, I'm in the middle of a series of seven injections, the first two being the painful intramuscular. I am in some danger apparently because I delayed going to the ER, and the risk of the bat drool carrying the rabies virus. If the disease starts after its incubation period which is usually long 4-8 weeks but can also be as short as a few days – the disease is nearly 100% fatal. The vaccination if given on schedule is 100% effective. And you must be vaccinated according to the Ulster County Department of Health if you even just touch a bat I’ve been getting out of the Health Alliance ER in the wee hours, which adds to the surreal mood. The nice nurses give me plenty of anecdotes and say a lot of people come in, many are from Ellenville for the vaccinations, including a young man who was feeding and playing with a raccoon until it bit him. My mistakes: First, according to Eve Walter, Ph.D. at the Ulster Department of Health, I should have collected the bat and brought him in for testing. If he tested negative, no vaccinations would have been needed, sparing me the pain and the county the expense. And I should not have delayed going to the ER on the off-chance my little bat was rabid – only 1% of our local bats carry the virus, but the nurse also asks if “he was acting normal?” “What is normal for a bat? I never found a bat on a sofa before. He was awfully passive and didn’t fly away when I let go." Was he sick or merely sleepy?I will know more in the next several weeks, but I feel you all should know there is no casual contact with a bat. In 2025, 95 people in Ulster County required rabies vaccinations. So far in 2026: 91. He can be as deadly as Nosferatu, or as he’s best known, Dracula. The only positive note is that the vaccinations are free.“You won’t be charged,” the night nurse called after me as I walked out into the dark of night.Laura Shaine Cunningham has written many plays and books, including A Place in the Country. analysis.time: Publication date: 2026-07-23. Event date: 4th of July (unspecified year, but context suggests recent).
analysis.location_and_population: Ulster County, New York, specifically Marbletown-Rosendale area. Affected individual: Laura Shaine Cunningham, a resident who had contact with a bat.
analysis.event: Confirmed bat contact incident requiring rabies postexposure prophylaxis (RPEP). Reported by the individual herself. The incident is confirmed, and the treatment is ongoing.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: One individual exposed. Risk is high due to potential rabies virus transmission from bat saliva. Rabies is nearly 100% fatal if symptoms develop, but vaccination is 100% effective if administered on schedule. In 2025, 95 people in Ulster County required rabies vaccinations.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Investigation and treatment ongoing. The bat was not tested, so rabies status is unknown. The individual is receiving a seven-injection RPEP series at HealthAlliance Hospital in Kingston, after delays in accessing the vaccine at Ellenville ER. The Ulster County Department of Health was involved, and authorization for treatment was obtained at 1 a.m. The source is a full original report.

analysis.brief_en: On July 4th, a Marbletown resident, Laura Shaine Cunningham, experienced a potentially dangerous health incident after picking up a live bat from her porch, mistaking it for a leaf. Despite the bat not biting her, the Ulster County Department of Health classified the contact as a rabies exposure risk, as bat saliva can transmit the nearly 100% fatal virus. After a delay in seeking treatment, Cunningham underwent a seven-injection rabies postexposure prophylaxis (RPEP) series at HealthAlliance Hospital in Kingston, following authorization from the health department. The incident highlights the severe risk of bat contact, even without a bite, and the importance of prompt medical attention. In 2025, 95 people in Ulster County required similar rabies vaccinations.

elements_zh.time: 发表日期:2026-07-23。事件日期:7月4日(年份未指明,但上下文表明为近期)。
elements_zh.location_and_population: 纽约州阿尔斯特县,特别是马布尔敦-罗森代尔地区。受影响的人:劳拉·谢恩·坎宁安 (Laura Shaine Cunningham),一位与蝙蝠有过接触的居民。
elements_zh.event: 已确认的蝙蝠接触事件需要 狂犬病 暴露后预防 (RPEP)。由该人本人举报。事件已确认,治疗 正在进行中。
elements_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: 一个人暴露了。由于蝙蝠唾液中存在潜在的 狂犬病病毒 传播,因此风险较高。如果出现症状,狂犬病 几乎 100% 致命,但如果按计划给药,疫苗接种 则 100% 有效。2025 年,阿尔斯特县有 95 人需要 狂犬病 疫苗接种。
elements_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: 调查和 治疗 正在进行中。该蝙蝠未经测试,因此 狂犬病 状态未知。在访问埃伦维尔急诊室的 疫苗 出现延误后,该患者正在金斯顿 HealthAlliance 医院接受七次 RPEP 系列注射。阿尔斯特县卫生部参与其中,并于凌晨 1 点获得了 治疗 的授权。来源是完整的原始报告。

news.source_body_en: On July 4th, a Marbletown resident, Laura Shaine Cunningham, experienced a potentially dangerous health incident after picking up a live bat from her porch, mistaking it for a leaf. Despite the bat not biting her, the Ulster County Department of Health classified the contact as a rabies exposure risk, as bat saliva can transmit the nearly 100% fatal virus. After a delay in seeking treatment, Cunningham underwent a seven-injection rabies postexposure prophylaxis (RPEP) series at HealthAlliance Hospital in Kingston, following authorization from the health department. The incident highlights the severe risk of bat contact, even without a bite, and the importance of prompt medical attention. In 2025, 95 people in Ulster County required similar rabies vaccinations.
news.content_zh: 7 月 4 日,马布尔敦 (Marbletown) 居民劳拉·谢恩·坎宁安 (Laura Shaine Cunningham) 从自家门廊捡起一只活蝙蝠,误以为是一片树叶,导致健康事故发生。尽管蝙蝠没有咬她,但阿尔斯特县卫生部仍将此次接触列为 狂犬病 暴露风险,因为蝙蝠唾液可以传播这种几乎 100% 致命的病毒。在延迟寻求 治疗 后,Cunningham 经卫生部门授权,在金斯顿 HealthAlliance 医院接受了七次注射 狂犬病 暴露后预防 (RPEP) 系列。这一事件凸显了即使没有被蝙蝠咬伤,与蝙蝠接触的严重风险,以及及时就医的重要性。2025 年,阿尔斯特县有 95 人需要类似的 狂犬病 疫苗接种。

news.content: ADVERTISEMENTNewsWeatherClosuresEventsPodcastsLISTENLISTEN26°C | 79°FCloseTop StoriesLocal NewsMidwestern OntarioSarniaWindsorSportsAgricultureEventsClosuresWeatherPodcastsPollResultsContactSubmit A News TipAdvertiseStay informed with our free daily newsletter, powered by DKI First Choice Disaster Restoration.Sign up(File photo courtesy of © Can Stock Photo / rabbit75can)ChathamNewsRise in wildlife encounters triggers CK Public Health precaution tipsBy Paul PedroJuly 24, 2026 - 4:02pmChatham-Kent Public Health (CKPH) is reminding the public to avoid direct contact with wildlife following an increase in "preventable encounters" with bats and raccoons.Public health officials said wildlife encounters are on the rise in Chatham-Kent and a growing number of people have required Rabies Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP), a series of treatments after a potential rabies exposure.Rabies is a serious viral disease that affects the nervous system and is almost always fatal once symptoms appear.The local health unit noted that cases of human rabies are rare and treatable with timely medical intervention, but added that avoiding contact with wildlife remains the best protection."Many of the recent wildlife encounters we've investigated were avoidable," said CKPH Healthy Environments Program Manager Joshua Standel. "Even animals that appear healthy, friendly, injured, or orphaned can carry rabies. We encourage residents to admire wildlife from a distance and never attempt to touch, feed, or handle wild animals."Officials noted that bats and raccoons are among the wildlife species most commonly associated with rabies exposures in Ontario and remind individuals to take the following precautions:Never touch, handle, or feed wild animals.Keep a safe distance from bats, raccoons, and other wildlife.Teach children to avoid approaching or touching wild animals.Ensure pets are up to date on their rabies vaccinations.Seek assistance from trained animal control or wildlife professionals if an animal appears sick, injured, or abandoned.CKPH said people who have been bitten or scratched by a wild animal, or who have had direct contact with a bat, should immediately wash the affected area thoroughly with soap and water and seek medical attention as soon as possible.Potential exposures should also be reported to CKPH for assessment and follow-up, officials noted."Protecting yourself and your family starts with keeping a respectful distance from wildlife," added Standel. "A simple decision not to touch a wild animal can help prevent the need for rabies treatment."Click here or contact CK Public Health at 519-352-7270 for more information about rabies prevention and what to do following a potential exposure.Read More Local StoriesScoreboard, July 25Sports10 hours agoThe Toronto Blue Jays lost the series opener in Boston 6-4Chatham Kent Beyond the Headlines episode 5: 'Dresden 1957' Director Eric PhilpottNews1 days agoOn this episode, host Jaryn Vecchio speaks to Eric Philpott, the director of the documentary 'Dresden 1957'.Blenheim man running in CK electionNews1 days agoFred Hooper is running in Ward 2, hoping to be one of two councillors representing people in Blenheim, Ridgetown, Erieau, and other communities.CK police chief calls 2025 crime decrease a significant achievementNews1 days agoThe crime severity index in Chatham-Kent dropped significantly last year, according to Statistics Canada.Headlocks for Hospice comes to Chatham this FridayNews1 days agoMaple Leaf Pro (MLP) Wrestling brings Headlocks for Hospice to Chatham in support of the Chatham-Kent Hospice Foundation.Hope Haven GM running in CK electionNews1 days agoLoree Bailey is running in Ward 5, hoping to be one of two representatives for people in Wallaceburg and the surrounding area.Load More Local Stories225-metre ship runs aground near Sarnia Harbour (GALLERY)CK News TodayUndoRetired Merlin farmer running in CK electionCK News TodayUndoAsk a Pro: "I'm 65 With $1.1M Saved.
